messages:
nina_ae: Client (NovaPayments) POC requirement: strict daily egress IP rotation for audit, but their firewall team will only whitelist 3 IPs at any time. They refuse to buy extra EIPs. Thoughts?

rachit_net: We have three practical approaches:
1) mTLS: issue short-lived client certs daily; customer whitelists a single control IP and validates certs. Satisfies audit rotation without IP churn.
2) Small reserved EIP set: give them 3 static EIPs we present, we rotate backend hosts behind them (doesn't meet "IP change daily" requirement).
3) Private network (VPC peering / Private deployment): no public IPs, best security, longer setup.

nina_ae: They insisted on "IPs must change daily" for compliance. Can mTLS produce equivalent evidence?

sam_sec: Yes. We can provide a signed daily rotation manifest and short-lived client certs rotated each day. Manifest contains mapping, timestamps, and signature; we also provide logs showing TLS client cert thumbprints for connections. That should satisfy auditors.

rachit_net: Operational ask for POC if they choose mTLS: provide contact for cert handshake, confirm whether they accept Redwood-issued client certs (faster) or want to supply a CA. Also need expected qps and which region for Dedicated endpoint so we can reserve capacity.

nina_ae: I'll propose mTLS-first with option to fall back to /29 allowlist if they insist on IP changes.

opsbot: Ticket POC-NOVA-77 created for network + security action items, assigned to rachit_net and sam_sec. SLA: 72h to deliver sample manifest and curl + openssl test steps.
